canon: M11: Spree Ender,Killed the enemy who was on a killing spree.,Kill.SpreeEnder
why: same whose-spree ambiguity as S25a/S25b, and the apostrophe contraction is not used elsewhere in the canon's terse Self-line register.
conveys the same single fact as S23a with no new information, so the trio does not provide the three-way variation the table pattern (e.g. S03a/S03b/S03c) relies on.

quote: You broke shields but only converted {shield_break_to_kill_conversion} of those breaks into kills — finish the fight before shields reset.
why: The value is interpolated raw with no unit (no '%' as used for accuracy_ar/accuracy_magnum) and the Threshold (0.5) is on a 0–1 scale while the table's other ratio-type fields (accuracy_ar: 20, accuracy_magnum: 25) are on a 0–100 scale, so either the line will read as an unnatural decimal ('converted 0.42 of those breaks') or the threshold comparison is on the wrong scale and the condition fires almost every match, undermining the 'one specific, earned correction' design.
fix: You broke shields but only converted {shield_break_to_kill_conversion}% of those breaks into kills — finish the fight before shields reset. (store/compare the backing stat on the same 0–100 scale as the accuracy fields, or explicitly document it as a 0–1 fraction and set Threshold accordingly)

quote: Dependable middle ground — no edge, no gap, just Marine's default numbers.
canon: B06 LOCKSTEP note: "Moves with the squad, nothing flashy — the baseline profile in a word."
why: IRONCLAD and LOCKSTEP both exist only to say 'this is the unmodified baseline profile,' so the two callsigns give Marine no distinct identities between them.
fix: Reground IRONCLAD in a specific tuning trait (e.g. its 900ms commit_window or 0.20 switch_margin) instead of restating 'default, nothing special.'

quote: Named for retreating, not engaging — matches Recruit's dulled StateTree behavior.
canon: B03 BACKSTOP note: "Last line, not first contact — suits the slowest, softest tuning row."
why: FALLBACK and BACKSTOP both encode the identical 'avoids first contact / falls back' persona, so the two Recruit callsigns don't provide distinguishable variation.
fix: Differentiate FALLBACK via a different tuning axis (e.g. its 120ms reaction_jitter or 2.0s target_memory_s) rather than repeating BACKSTOP's 'avoids engagement' theme.
